title: Regular-expression denial of service (ReDoS)
root_cause: A backtracking regex engine tries alternative ways to match; with nested or overlapping quantifiers the number of alternatives grows exponentially with input length. A tiny hostile input therefore consumes unbounded CPU. Java, JavaScript, Python, Ruby, PHP and .NET engines are all affected, and the bug sits in validation code, not in the engine.
defenses: Avoid nested quantifiers and overlapping alternations such as (a+)+, (a|a)*, (.*)*.
Cap the length of untrusted input before it reaches a regex.
Use a linear-time engine (RE2, Rust regex, Go regexp) for untrusted input.
Set match timeouts where the runtime supports them (.NET, Java 9+ patterns, Node worker threads).
Lint patterns in CI with a ReDoS detector.
